Nduagu, E., Sow, A., Umeozor, E. and Millington, D. (2017). Economic Potentials and Efficiencies of Oil Sands Operations: Processes and Technologies. Canadian Energy Research Institute, Study No. 164, Calgary, Alberta, March 2017. ISBN 1-927037-49-2.

Loaded: SAGD base case (capex with breakdown in other-values, fixed and chemical opex, gas, direct emissions); reservoir technologies (Nsolv pure solvent, generic steam-solvent, SAP, SA-SAGD, ESEIEH, RF XL, SEGD, steam-surfactant), steam generation (OTSG at 78% and SQ90 at 90% quality from Table 2.4, DCSG, SOFC, GT-OTSG) and the delayed coking upgrader benchmark plus six partial or deep upgrading technologies (EJS, CCC, DSU, IYQ, HTL, Hi-Q) from Table 2.7 and the text; Tables A.1-A.4 for capex and opex details; measures with numbers (Tables 2.1, 2.4, 2.8, 2.9) in the measures file. Not loaded: water/wastewater and business management technologies beyond the measures list, pipeline technologies (Armadillo, Spectrum XLI, SmartBall), supply-cost, emissions and production forecasts of Chapter 4 beyond other-values, the innovation-ecosystem appendix, and the mining/CSS cases (Study 164 treats in situ only). Figures 4.1, 4.2 and 4.6 give segment ranges or chart positions, so only printed range labels are in other-values. Locator convention: printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 18). PRICE YEAR: study base year is real 2015 Canadian dollars (Nelson-Farrar indices; US$ at C$1 = US$0.85, p.53); 2002 and 2013 values are labelled as printed; US$ antenna costs carry no year (2017 assumed, flagged). Traps: (1) capex quoted per bbl/d of bitumen feed capacity; the upgrader outputs 26,500 bbl/d SCO from 30,000 bbl/d bitumen, so per bbl of SCO is 13% higher; (2) Table 2.7 internal inconsistencies: DSU capex 511.7 M (17,057 per bbl/d) vs 35,000 per bbl/d in the text; DSU 33 kWh/bbl vs 19.2 from 8 MW per 10,000 bbl/d; EJS 2 kWh/bbl vs 3.4 from 4,261 kW; Hi-Q emissions 57 kgCO2e/bbl said to be 20% below coking but coker is 132 kgCO2/bbl (extraction excluded for upgrading rows; the Fig. 4.6 totals add the 60.4 SAGD base); (3) Table 2.6 prints SAGD electricity as 300 kWh/day, a typo for MWh/d; (4) Table A.4 total variable expenses 288.9 M/yr cannot be reproduced from the printed quantities and prices; (5) capex and gas-use rows for Nsolv, steam-solvent, ESEIEH and SEGD are derived from printed percentage changes against the SAGD base and flagged in the notes; (6) the ESEIEH opex currency is not marked (C$ assumed); (7) Table 2.6 attaches SAGD CAPEX of 30,000-50,000 per barrel to the SEGD row; (8) emissions are direct fuel and electricity only (no flaring or fugitive).
